title: loss-detecting structured log ingress with trace-fidelity and adaptive backpressure
creator: Alex Kim
description:
Summary:
We will implement a resilient structured-log ingress path that prioritizes correlation-id fidelity and detects message loss early, enabling safe replay and adaptive backpressure across Loki and ELK sinks. This ticket covers the protocol-level sequence tagging, ingress-side watermarking, loss detectors, canonical correlation-id normalization, and producer/sidecar deployment strategy.

Goals:
- Ensure >99.95% preservation of correlation IDs across the ingest pipeline for traced requests.
- Surface loss metrics within 60s of occurrence and enable automated replay for recoverable gaps.
- Provide adaptive backpressure signals to producers (sidecars and SDKs) before queue saturation to protect SLOs.
- Maintain compatibility with existing Loki/Elasticsearch outputs and the Console dashboards.

Scope & non-goals:
In scope: structured log schema extension (sequence-ticket), ingress preprocessor (loss-detector), exporter adapters, Grafana/Loki dashboards, alerts and runbook updates, rollout plan with feature flags.
Out of scope: wholesale consumer-side reprocessing systems and long-term cold-storage re-ingest flows (separate initiative).

Design overview:
1) Sequence-tagged envelopes: producers/sidecars attach a monotonic sequence_ticket per stream (tenant+source), plus epoch for connector restarts. Ingress will maintain a rolling per-source ack-window.
2) Fast-loss detector: a streaming operator computes gaps in sequence_ticket; small transient gaps (<3 items or <2s) are treated as 'transient-miss' and annotated; larger gaps tripped to 'loss-detected' with a hypothesis id and retention for replay.
3) Trace-fidelity canonicalizer: correlation_id normalization policy (trim, hex-normalize, canonical-uuid fallback) and fallback to span-link enrichment via OTEL span-links when correlation_id missing but trace context present.
4) Adaptive backpressure: ingress exposes a pushback API (HTTP 429 Retry-After + X-RW-Backpressure header) consumed by sidecars/SDKs; high-latency/queue-depth triggers sampling-mode where only header-level telemetry is accepted.
5) Multi-sink consistency: loss annotations are persisted as structured fields, and exporters to Loki/ES include loss.status/loss.hypothesis fields to allow dashboarding and downstream reconciliation.

Trade-offs considered:
- Adding sequence tickets increases payload size and producer complexity; we adopt a compact base64-encoded 8-byte token to minimize overhead.
- Aggressive replay risks duplicate events; to mitigate duplicates we add event_fingerprint and use idempotent append semantics where supported.
- Backpressure uplinks increase producer coupling; we make the backpressure API optional and default to a graceful sampling policy if producers do not honor signals.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (canary): enable sequence-tag acceptance and passive loss detection in canary region (1% traffic). Metrics only, no backpressure.
- Phase 1: deploy sidecar SDK update to emit sequence_ticket (opt-in). Enable loss annotations and dashboarding (observability-2.8).
- Phase 2: opt-in backpressure signals for sidecars; enable automated sampling-mode for selected high-throughput tenants.
- Phase 3: wide rollout and enable replay tooling for gaps classified as recoverable.

Metrics & dashboards:
New metrics: ingress.sequence_gap_rate, ingress.loss_detected_rate, ingress.replay_requests, ingress.backpressure_signals_sent, ingress.latency_p50/p95/p99. Thresholds and alerts: pager if loss_detected_rate > 0.1% sustained for 5m and correlation-preservation drops below 99.9%. Dashboards will be added to Console under Observability -> Ingest -> Loss & Trace Fidelity (Grafana + Loki query panels).

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for canonicalizer and gap detection logic.
- Integration tests deploying sidecar in staging with synthetic gap injection harness.
- Chaos test to simulate broker replay and verify idempotency.
- Load test to verify backpressure reduces queue depth and preserves latency SLOs.

Docs & runbooks:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/LDI+-+Loss+Detecting+Ingress (draft)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/12345 (preliminary implementation)
- Runbook: alert -> triage -> enable sampling-mode -> replay window -> postmortem.

Acceptance criteria:
- Passive canary detects injected gaps and creates loss annotations with <=30s detection latency.
- Sidecar-instrumented tenants honor backpressure in 90% of signals in Phase 2.
- Dashboards show loss metrics and there is a non-interrupting path to request replays for recoverable gaps.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define canonical event_fingerprint algorithm to minimize false duplicate matches (security review for content hashing).
- Finalize storage TTL for loss hypotheses to balance replayability vs cost.
- Evaluate trade-offs of persistent per-source state vs stateless watermark estimation for horizontal scaling.
